rulings.raw: 2 Tablespoons Olive Oil or Avocado Oil Divided
rulings.evidence: Either/or line taken as olive oil: olive-oil is a live board id at 7 of 7 (precedent 'extra-virgin olive oil' -> olive-oil, 2026-08-26), so a REUSE and not a proposal. The board's `avocados` hit is a form flip - the fruit is not the oil, different price class and different gram weight.

rulings.raw: ½ Fresh Lime or Orange Juiced
rulings.evidence: Instructions use lime ('the juice of half a lime'), so the orange option is not taken; precedent 'fresh lime juice' -> limes (2026-08-27) on vocabulary row Lime Juice [limes], fresh fruit squeezed rather than a bottled juice. Half a lime yields about 15 g.

Board ABSENT for the phrase; a Cajun-style paprika/cayenne blend, not the `seasoned-salt` of the 2026-08-26 precedent (different blend, different jar). New id proposed - registrar should check cajun-seasoning/creole-seasoning as possible existing spellings.

REFUSED the bridge onto `rice`: dry rice is a different price class and roughly a third of the cooked weight, the standing form-flip rejection. Prepared frozen pouch, weighed as two 10 oz bags since the source names no package size.

rulings.raw: Primal Kitchen Avocado Lime Dipping Sauce Drizzled to Garnish
rulings.evidence: Optional brand-specific garnish ('if using' in the instructions); dropped rather than made a new niche commodity, so the shopper buys nothing for it. The board's `avocados` match is a different food.

db_row_notes: blackened-chicken-with-mango-salsa: 'Lime Juice' arrived on a different serving basis (100 g = 100 g) than the row the DB holds, and the two AGREE once put on one basis - the mapper's row scaled onto the DB's 1 tbsp = 15 g reproduces the DB's own numbers within 5 kcal and 0.5 g. Nothing was written and the household row stands, which is the rule.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Cajun-style blackening blend (paprika, cayenne, garlic, salt) sold as its own jar by McCormick, Zatarain's and store brands. The table reports board ABSENT: no commodity and no capture match. The only near precedent is `seasoned-salt` (2026-08-26), a different blend with no chile heat and a different jar, so not an alias. I cannot read the namespaces myself: if an id already prices this food it will be spelled cajun-seasoning or creole-seasoning, and either of those should ALIAS rather than mint.

Prepared frozen rice pouch (Path of Life, Trader Joe's, store brands), the recipe's whole carbohydrate source at 567 g source scale. Not `rice`: dry rice is a different price class and about a third the weight per cup, the standing form-flip rejection, and `wild-rice`/`rice-vinegar` are different foods. If the estate already prices prepared frozen rice under frozen-rice or cooked-rice, alias onto it - the cilantro-lime flavour does not warrant a second id.

registrar_rulings.reason: Same food, same form, already priced: cajun-seasoning is labeled 'Cajun / Creole Seasoning' and is live at $0.1666/oz (7 stores); the match baseline already assigns 'Louisiana Fish Fry Blackened Cajun Seasoning' to it, and the Zatarain's/Tone's 'Blackened Seasoning' jars sit <unmatched> only because the include patterns lack the spelling — a blackening blend is the same Cajun-class jar, not a variant. Follow-up: add blackened-seasoning -> cajun-seasoning to recipe-floor-id-map.json and extend cajun-seasoning's includes with blackened\s+seasoning (guarding against blackened salmon/chicken/turkey/alfredo product names) via add-commodity-rule.ps1.

No existing id prices prepared frozen rice: the prepared-rice estate is per-variety (cooked-jasmine-rice requires 'jasmine'; ready-to-serve-long-grain-wild-rice-pouch explicitly EXCLUDES both 'frozen' and 'cilantro' at commodities.json:68769-70, so the estate has already ruled these out of the existing rows), dry 'rice' is the standing form-flip rejection, and the id has no feed cell. Mint as recipe-only (recipe-board baseline + recipe-commodities.json), together with allowlist pairs vs rice, cooked-jasmine-rice, and ready-to-serve-long-grain-wild-rice-pouch, contiguous includes like cilantro\s*lime\s+rice with a frozen/prepared context, and ~150-pattern-grade excludes including cauliflower (frozen cilantro-lime cauliflower rice is a different food), dressing, salad, bowl, burrito, meal kit, dry/uncooked/rice mix.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS on the sharp instrument. Protein 43.6 vs 40 is +9%, inside the 15% band, and it comes almost entirely from 680.4 g of chicken breast - 170 g raw per serving at the 14-serving scale, right on the catalog's 167 g average across 80 live chicken-breast recipes, so the main-protein each-weight is not the failure mode here.
macro_cross_check.divergence: Calories +17% and carbs +77% against the published figures, and the whole gap is the one line the source never quantified: '2 Packages Frozen Cilantro Lime Rice' with no package size printed anywhere on the page. Their own numbers back-solve almost exactly to 2 CUPS of prepared rice (280 g), which recomputes to about 498 cal / 41.6 g protein / 39 g carbs - i.e. the source's recipe-card plugin appears to have read 'package' as one serving. I weighed the line the way it is printed instead, at two 10 oz pouches (567 g), because that is what a reader buying 'two packages' actually gets. Both readings clear this run's band (450-800 cal, protein >= 40), so the recipe advances either way, but flag it: if the 10 oz pouch assumption is wrong the calorie figure moves and nothing downstream will catch it.
